nodes.notes: 1) Classification: fused transformer block (LN+QKV+attn+softmax+proj+residual+LN+MLP(GELU)+residual) over 4x4 windows on (1,720,1280,32). num_heads=1, C=32, N=16. 2) Math: per window of 16 tokens, Q,K,V = xW_qkv+b (in C=32 channels); attn=softmax(QK^T/sqrt(C)+rpe); out=attn*V; proj; residual; LN2; fc1 32->128; GELU; fc2 128->32; residual. 3) Layout: x is (B,H,W,C) contiguous; window partition reshapes H,W into (nH,Wh,nW,Ww). For Wh=Ww=4, windows are 4x4 contiguous in W but strided in H by W*C. There are 180*320=57600 windows total. 4) Regimes: (a) Bandwidth-bound full block (likely dominant): IO ~236MB, lower bound ~0.26ms; (b) Compute-bound if MLP hidden=128 dominates: 16*32*128 + 16*128*32 = 131K FMA/window * 57600 = 7.5G FMA = ~0.24ms at peak FP16 FMA; (c) Sync/latency-bound if too many barriers or tiny dispatch. 5) Knobs: threadgroup = one window (16 threads, one per token) or multiple windows per group; weights in groupshared loaded once per group (qkv 6KB, proj 2KB, fc1 8KB, fc2 8KB = 24KB total, fits <32KB); rpe 256*2=512B; per-token vector in registers (C=32 -> 32 fp16 regs, hidden=128 -> 128 fp16 regs ~ 64 regs). Softmax via wave intrinsics over 16-lane subgroup. LN reductions via wave ops. 6) Skeleton: one threadgroup = one or few windows; threads=16 per window mapped to tokens; load weights cooperatively into groupshared once per group; each thread holds its token vector in regs; LN1 (wave reduce), compute Q,K,V (matmul against shared weights), exchange K,V via groupshared, compute attn row, softmax (wave reduce), accumulate attn*V in regs, proj into out, add residual, LN2 (wave reduce), fc1->GELU->fc2 in regs, add residual, write out. 7) Families: (F1) Full-fusion per-window threadgroup with weights in groupshared and tokens in registers — TOP candidate, single dispatch, no global round-trip; (F2) Split kernels (attn then MLP) — rejected: blocked by single-dispatch constraint and would double IO; (F3) Multi-window per group to amortize weight loads further — viable refinement. Working set per window: 16 tokens * 32 fp16 = 1KB activations (in regs across 16 threads); shared = weights 24KB (read-only reusable tile, producer=all threads cooperative, consumer=all threads, reuse = #windows_per_group * many ops, barrier only after load). Decision: F1 with multi-window groups.

action.description: Implement a single-dispatch fused kernel where each threadgroup processes one 4x4 window with 16 threads (one per token). Load all small weights (qkv, proj, fc1, fc2, norms, rpe) into groupshared once at kernel start. Each thread keeps its token vector in registers through LN1->QKV->attn->proj->residual->LN2->MLP->residual. Use wave intrinsics for LN reductions and softmax (16-lane active). Exchange K and V across the 16 threads via small groupshared buffers.
action.rationale: Maximizes fusion (no global round-trips between LN/attn/MLP), keeps per-token activations in registers, amortizes weight loads across 16 tokens per group. Approaches bandwidth lower bound of ~0.26ms.
action.title: Per-window fused threadgroup, weights in groupshared, tokens in registers

kernel_summary: Fused simplified Swin transformer block over input (1,720,1280,32) fp16 with 4x4 non-shifted windows, single head, channels C=32, hidden=128. Per-window work is tiny (N=16 tokens) and weights are small (~24KB total), making the kernel strongly bandwidth-bound (lower bound ~0.26 ms for the 236 MB activation IO). The right strategy is full single-dispatch fusion: one threadgroup per window (or several windows), 16 threads per window with each thread owning one token vector in registers; load all weights once into groupshared as a read-only reusable tile; perform LN1, QKV projection, scaled QK^T+rpe, softmax, attn*V, proj, residual, LN2, fc1, GELU, fc2, residual entirely without round-tripping intermediates to global memory. Wave intrinsics handle LN mean/var reductions and softmax max/sum across the 16 tokens.
open_questions: Are 16-lane partial wave reductions reliable on Blackwell DXIL, or should we use groupshared scratch for per-window reductions when packing multiple windows per warp?
How are fp16 buffer loads exposed in cs_6_8 (Buffer<float16_t> vs ByteAddressBuffer with f16tof32)?
Does LayerNorm need fp32 accumulation to meet rtol=0.01/atol=0.01 given fp16 stats?
Is GELU expected to match torch's exact (erf-based) or tanh approximation under the given tolerance?
How is bias rpe broadcast applied — is the (1,1,16,16) bias shared identically across all windows? (yes, per spec)
Are 57600 threadgroups optimal, or should we pack multiple windows per group to better amortize weight loads and fully utilize 32-lane warps?
Does the runner support cs_6_8 fp16 native types, or do we need to manually pack/unpack via uint32?
What is the actual reference latency baseline so we can size expected_vs_baseline_factor sensibly?
